name: The Familiar
concept_focus: Build an AI agent from scratch: a chat loop, a brain, tools, an act-observe loop, planning, memory and guardrails

story.title: The Familiar
story.client: Archivist Wren of the Hunters' Guild
story.hook: Every guild hunter wants a familiar: a helper that listens, uses tools, remembers and plans. Wren will teach you to bind one in plain Python, piece by piece. She also warns you about the last familiar the guild bound, which learned to ignore its limits. It is still out there.

acts.title: Act I: A Voice
acts.goal: A familiar that listens and answers: a chat loop, a history and a simple rule-based brain behind one interface.

acts.title: Act II: Hands
acts.goal: Give it tools: a safe calculator, a tool registry, notes on disk, and the act-observe loop that lets the brain use them.

acts.title: Act III: A Mind
acts.goal: Plans for multi-step goals, a memory it can search, state it can save and resume, and a scripted brain for testing.

acts.title: Act IV: Leash and Lightning
acts.goal: Guardrails and an evaluation harness, an optional real language-model brain, and the finished familiar.

boss_lore: The Rogue Familiar was never cruel. It was simply given tools without a leash and goals without a limit.
boss_brief: Bring a finished agent.py: a chat loop with history, a swappable brain, a tool registry with a safe calculator and notes, an act-observe loop with a step limit, planning and searchable memory, guardrails with confirmations and an action log, and an evaluation harness that passes with your scripted brain.

mobs.name: The Silent Familiar
mobs.encounter: Make a program that keeps talking until you tell it to stop.
mobs.contract: Your familiar has been bound, but it will not speak. Give it a voice: it waits, it listens, it answers, and it knows when you have said goodbye.

objectives.label: Open the conversation
objectives.brief: In agent.py, write a loop that reads a line from the user, prints a reply and repeats.

objectives.label: Say goodbye
objectives.brief: End the conversation cleanly on quit, exit or bye, in any capitalisation, with a farewell.

objectives.label: Handle silence
objectives.brief: Make empty input and stray spaces harmless, and explain what your loop did with them before.

mobs.name: The Echoing Memory
mobs.concept: A conversation history as a list of dictionaries
mobs.encounter: Keep every message with who said it.
mobs.contract: A familiar that forgets what you said a moment ago is a parrot. Give it a history: every message, and who spoke it.

objectives.label: Keep the history
objectives.brief: Store every turn in a list of dictionaries with a role (user or familiar) and the content.

objectives.label: Show recent turns
objectives.brief: Add a history command that prints the last few turns, numbered, with who said each one.

objectives.label: Explain the shape
objectives.brief: Explain why each message is a dictionary with a role instead of a plain string, and what that makes possible later.

mobs.name: The Keyword Brain
mobs.concept: Intents from keywords, with a fallback
mobs.encounter: Answer by spotting what the user wants.
mobs.contract: Before your familiar can think, it can notice. Teach it to spot what you are asking for from the words you use, and to admit when it has no idea.

objectives.label: Map words to intents
objectives.brief: Use a dictionary from intents (greeting, help, time, thanks) to their keywords, pick the intent a message matches and reply for it.

objectives.label: Clean the words
objectives.brief: Lower-case the message and strip punctuation before matching, so Hello!! still counts as a greeting.

objectives.label: Fix the hidden match
objectives.brief: Explain why checking whether 'hi' is in the message wrongly matches 'this' or 'which', and match whole words instead.

objectives.label: Admit confusion
objectives.brief: Give a helpful fallback reply when nothing matches, suggesting what the user can ask.

mobs.name: The Brain Socket
mobs.concept: Swapping behaviour behind one function interface
mobs.encounter: Separate the loop from the brain that decides the reply.
mobs.contract: Wren's first rule of binding: the body and the brain are separate. Build a socket where any brain can sit, and your familiar can be upgraded without being rebuilt.

objectives.label: Build the socket
objectives.brief: Make the chat loop call a brain function that receives the history and returns the reply, instead of deciding the reply itself.

objectives.label: Swap brains
objectives.brief: Write a second, different brain (for example one that answers in riddles) and let the user switch brains with a command.

objectives.label: Explain the socket
objectives.brief: Explain why the loop must not care which brain is plugged in, and which brain you will plug in later in this campaign.

mobs.name: The Calculator Imp
mobs.encounter: Give the familiar a calculator tool that never runs code.
mobs.contract: Imps love arithmetic and they love tricks more. Give your familiar a calculator that understands sums and refuses to run anything else you hand it.

objectives.label: Parse a sum
objectives.brief: Write a calculator tool that understands a number, an operator (+, -, *, /) and a number, and returns the answer as text.

objectives.label: Refuse to run code
objectives.brief: Explain why calling eval on user text is dangerous, and show your tool rejects input that is not a simple sum.

objectives.label: Return errors as text
objectives.brief: Return a clear message for division by zero or a malformed sum instead of crashing the familiar.

mobs.name: The Tool Ledger
mobs.concept: A registry of tools as data
mobs.encounter: List every tool with what it does, and call any of them by name.
mobs.contract: A familiar with hands needs a ledger of what each hand can hold. Write every tool down by name, with a description and the arguments it takes.

objectives.label: Write the ledger
objectives.brief: Keep a dictionary from tool names to their function, a one-line description and the names of the arguments they need. Add a clock tool alongside the calculator.

objectives.label: Call a tool by name
objectives.brief: Write run_tool(name, args) that looks the tool up, calls it with a dictionary of arguments and returns its result.

objectives.label: Handle a missing tool
objectives.brief: Return a clear result for an unknown tool or missing arguments, and add a tools command that lists the ledger.

mobs.name: The Decision Spirit
mobs.encounter: Let the brain choose between replying and using a tool, then see the result.
mobs.contract: This is the heart of every agent. The spirit decides: answer now, or reach for a tool, look at what came back, and decide again.

objectives.label: Shape a decision
objectives.brief: Make the brain return either a reply or a tool request (a tool name and its arguments) as a dictionary.

objectives.label: Act, observe, repeat
objectives.brief: When the brain asks for a tool, run it, add the result to the history as a tool message and ask the brain again, until it replies.

objectives.label: Set a step limit
objectives.brief: Explain what happens if a brain keeps asking for tools forever, and stop the loop after a set number of steps with an honest message.

mobs.name: The Scribe's Quill
mobs.encounter: Give the familiar notes that survive a restart.
mobs.contract: A familiar that cannot write things down is a familiar that cannot help tomorrow. Give it a quill and a book.

objectives.label: Write a note
objectives.brief: Add a save_note tool that stores a note with the date and time in a JSON file.

objectives.label: Read the notes
objectives.brief: Add tools to list every note and to find notes containing a word.

objectives.label: Survive a broken book
objectives.brief: Make a missing or corrupted notes file harmless, and explain what your tools do in each case.

mobs.name: The Planner Wisp
mobs.encounter: Turn one goal into a plan and carry it out step by step.
mobs.contract: Ask the familiar for something big and it freezes. The Wisp teaches it to break a goal into steps, do them in order, and tick them off.

objectives.label: Make a plan
objectives.brief: When given a goal, have the brain produce a list of steps, each one a tool call or a reply, and show the plan to the user.

objectives.label: Follow the plan
objectives.brief: Carry the plan out step by step through the act-observe loop, marking each step done and showing progress.

objectives.label: Recover from a failed step
objectives.brief: When a step fails, record why and either retry it, skip it or revise the remaining plan, and tell the user which.

mobs.name: The Long Memory
mobs.concept: Storing and retrieving facts by relevance
mobs.encounter: Remember facts and recall the ones that matter now.
mobs.contract: History is everything that was said. Memory is what is worth keeping. Teach your familiar to remember facts and recall the right ones when they matter.

objectives.label: Remember a fact
objectives.brief: Add a remember tool that stores facts the user teaches it, saved between runs.

objectives.label: Recall by relevance
objectives.brief: Score every stored fact by how many words it shares with the current message and give the brain the top three.

objectives.label: Predict a recall
objectives.brief: Given three stored facts and a question, predict which ones your scoring returns first, then check it.

mobs.name: The Scratchpad
mobs.concept: Agent state you can save and resume
mobs.encounter: Keep the goal, plan and progress in one state object that survives a restart.
mobs.contract: Familiars get interrupted. Give yours a scratchpad: the goal, the plan, what is done and what it noticed, all in one place you can put down and pick up.

objectives.label: Gather the state
objectives.brief: Keep the agent's goal, plan, completed steps, scratch notes and step count together in one dictionary or class.

objectives.label: Save and resume
objectives.brief: Save the state to disk and let the familiar resume an unfinished goal after a restart.

objectives.label: Explain the scratchpad
objectives.brief: Explain what would break if this state were spread across loose variables instead of kept together.

mobs.name: The Mock Oracle
mobs.concept: Testing an agent with a scripted brain
mobs.encounter: Write a brain that follows a script, and test the agent with it.
mobs.contract: You cannot test a familiar whose mind changes every run. The Mock Oracle speaks only from a script, so you can check the body does exactly what it should.

objectives.label: Write the scripted brain
objectives.brief: Write a MockBrain that returns a prepared list of decisions in order, so a whole conversation plays out the same every time.

objectives.label: Test three scenarios
objectives.brief: Write tests with assert that use MockBrain to check a plain reply, a tool call and the step limit.

objectives.label: Explain the mock
objectives.brief: Explain why a scripted brain makes the agent loop testable, and what it cannot tell you.

mobs.name: The Leash
mobs.encounter: Make dangerous tools ask first, and log everything.
mobs.contract: The Rogue Familiar deleted the guild's archive because nobody told it to ask first. Put a leash on yours: some tools need permission, every action is written down.

objectives.label: Mark the dangerous tools
objectives.brief: Give each tool a safety level in the ledger, and add a delete_note tool marked as dangerous.

objectives.label: Ask before acting
objectives.brief: Before running a dangerous tool, show the user exactly what will happen and run it only on a clear yes.

objectives.label: Log every action
objectives.brief: Append every tool call, its arguments, its result and the time to a log file, and add a log command to show recent entries.

mobs.name: The Judge of Answers
mobs.concept: Evaluating an agent against test tasks
mobs.encounter: Measure how often the familiar does the right thing.
mobs.contract: A familiar that seems to work is not one that works. The Judge sets it a list of tasks with known answers and counts how many it gets right.

objectives.label: Write the cases
objectives.brief: Write at least eight evaluation cases: a message, plus what a correct outcome looks like (a reply containing a word, or a particular tool being called).

objectives.label: Run the evaluation
objectives.brief: Run the agent on every case with a fresh state each time and report the pass rate.

objectives.label: Explain the failures
objectives.brief: For each failing case, print what was expected and what happened, and explain what you would change first.

mobs.name: The Lightning Bottle
mobs.concept: A language-model brain behind the same socket
mobs.encounter: Optionally plug a real language model into the brain socket, with your own key.
mobs.contract: Wren keeps lightning in a bottle: a real language model. It fits the socket you built in Act I. Plug it in if you want to; your familiar must work just as well without it.

objectives.label: Bottle the lightning
objectives.brief: Write an LLMBrain with the same interface as your other brains that sends the history to a language model, for example with the anthropic Python package. Install and configure it yourself; the game never asks for or stores a key.

objectives.label: Keep the key safe
objectives.brief: Read the API key only from an environment variable you set yourself, never print, save or hard-code it, and fall back to the keyword brain when it is missing or the network fails. Explain each case.

objectives.label: Describe tools to the model
objectives.brief: Describe your ledger's tools to the model and turn its tool requests back into run_tool calls, through the same act-observe loop.

mobs.name: The Familiar's Day
mobs.encounter: Show the finished familiar doing a real job from start to finish.
mobs.contract: Wren wants to see a full day's work before she signs your binding. One goal, start to finish: plan, tools, memory, notes, leash and log.

objectives.label: Run a full session
objectives.brief: Make one goal (for example: work out a budget and save it as a note) run end to end with planning, tools, memory and logging.

objectives.label: Write the help
objectives.brief: Add a help command that explains every command and tool in plain words.

objectives.label: Walk Wren through it
objectives.brief: Explain, step by step, how a message travels through your familiar: loop, brain, tools, memory, leash and back.
